question.text: Under the SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, the use of derivatives by a discretionary portfolio manager is principally restricted to:

answer.text: Hedging and portfolio rebalancing, subject to the Portfolio Management Agreement and disclosure-document requirements

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook permits portfolio managers to invest in derivatives, including for hedging and portfolio rebalancing, on recognised stock exchanges. Such investments must be set out in the Portfolio Management Agreement (including exposure details) and disclosed in the disclosure document. They are not a vehicle for unrestricted speculation or leveraged trading. The Trap: "Speculation and arbitrage freely" and "unlimited leveraged trading" both ignore the agreement-level exposure limits and disclosure obligations. "Prohibited entirely" is also wrong - hedging and rebalancing through derivatives are explicitly permitted. Note: Source - NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers Certification Examination workbook (Sep 2025), p. 108.
